newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Amsterdam cargo industry want fuel surcharge lifteD.
newsitem.headline: Amsterdam cargo industry want fuel surcharge lifteD.

text.p: Amsterdam's air cargo forwarders and general sales agents are again calling for a withdrawal of the fuel surcharge, following the latest round of airline rates increases.

KLM Royal Dutch Airlines announced yesterday that it will be increasing rates to the Middle East, Asia, India and U.S. from March 1. Rises vary, but are up to 30 percent on some routes. The airline stated that the Dutch guilder cents fuel surcharge would also remain in place.

Spokesman for the Dutch Airfreight Forwarders Association, Hans Knuvers, said that the organisation was under the impression that the rates rises would replace the fuel surcharges and not be in addition to them.
However, he did acknowledge that there did need to be some increases in the market. "Everyone is looking for a healthier situation and the airlines deserve and honest living," Knuvers said.
"The question is, will all the carriers in the Dutch market now follow?" he added.

ChartAir, director, Jos Busscher, said he could understand the need for higher rates as it was now vital to remain competitive in the industry. However, regarding the fact a fuel surcharge remains in place, he commented: "It is a very competitive market at the moment. The fight is on for the large accounts especially. If the KLM rates are not defendable in the market place, shippers will transfer their freight on to the ocean or look for other carriers."

Jan Van der Woensel, owner of general sales agent, Zygene, said despite the fact the company represents the airlines, not all of the GSA's airlines supported the fuel surcharge. Many feel it is not the right mechanism for an increase, he said.
LOT Polish Airlines had felt it was extremely impractical and unfair, because the same rate should be charged for a distance between Minsk and Warsaw as Warsaw to Beijing, he added.
Another carrier the company represents is Delta Airlines. Van der Woensel said the U.S. carrier was in the process of analysing what it will do concerning the surcharge.
"An increase of cargo rates of five to ten percent, depending on the area is acceptable, the market can sustain this. Forget the fuel surcharge," he stressed.

But he added that a rates increase should be maintained with every shipper, whether dealing with a small or large shipper, if the rates rises are to be a worthwhile exercise in improving market stability. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
